messages:
maria: FYI the perf eval harness for the new quantized model (quant-gpt7k-v1) is returning ~30% lower throughput in CI vs local, and cost/token is up ~25%. Dashboards disagree with local benches.

sam: are we seeing steady p95 regressions or tail (p99) spikes?

maria: mostly lower overall RPS in CI, p95 is sometimes fine but p99 spikes under sustained load. Local binary + config reproduces good numbers.

hao: sounds like a batching window behavior under contention. Fairshare or prefetch could be shrinking effective batching opportunities during bursts.

jess: can you paste the exact runner config the CI used?

maria: pasted config: https://paste.internal/xyz789

```json
{\n  "model": "quant-gpt7k-v1",\n  "batching_mode": "auto",\n  "batch_window_ms": 10,\n  "max_batch_size": 64,\n  "fairshare": true,\n  "kv_prefetch": true\n}
```

eval-bot: CI job perf-eval/throughput #457 failed — missing p95_latency in summary :warning:

sam: missing p95 usually means aggregator emitted NaN or metric was filtered. We had a bug where tokens-per-batch ended up zero and we divide by zero when computing per-token latencies.

maria: CI logs show many early client disconnects: `client disconnected before response` and `runner canceled batch (reason: steal)`.

hao: that aligns with a race: fairshare stealing can cause a window to close with no allocated tokens (empty batch), aggregator didn't guard against zero token_count.

jess: I wrote a small stress script that spawns load and randomly kills clients to reproduce. Repro steps attached.

maria: stress snippet:
```bash
# spawn 120 clients with random disconnects
for i in $(seq 1 120); do
  python3 stress_client.py --model quant-gpt7k-v1 &
  sleep 0.01
done
# randomly kill ~10% after 2s
sleep 2
pkill -f stress_client.py -n 12
```

sam: quick mitigation: guard aggregator denominator. If total_tokens == 0, skip sample and mark batch as cancelled. I pushed PR 1299 with the guard and unit tests.

maria: PR 1299 merged, CI throughput check turned green. I also added an alert for cost_per_token > 20% baseline so we'll catch this early.

jess: I'll change the ETL to convert NaN metrics to null so dashboards don't show zeros, and add an anomaly band for sudden cost jumps.

maria: despite the fix, nightly saturation sweeps still show p99 spikes around 85-92% utilization.

hao: I correlated those spikes with KV-prefetch: sometimes a prefetch request for a long prompt blocks the head of the batch and causes tail latency spikes. Suggest adding small random jitter to prefetch timing or deprioritizing prefetch when batch pressure is high.

sam: good lead. I'll build a replay harness to play CI traces with disconnects and long-prep requests so we can test prefetch changes deterministically. Will instrument batch sizes per window.

jess: also proposing a CI canary that runs with `batching_mode: fixed` alongside `auto` so any regression from auto heuristics surfaces quickly.

maria: created a short triage meeting invite. Please join: 2026-03-02 11:00 PT. Agenda: decide on prefetch throttling, aggregator hardening, and canary wiring.

eval-bot: calendar invite created — perf-ml/triage-1799001111 — 2026-03-02T18:00Z

sam: ack  prepping replay harness + metrics dump

jess: ack  updating ETL and adding canary pipeline

hao: ack  will prototype prefetch jitter and run local sweep

maria: leaving repro notes and CI artifact link in PR 1299. Thanks all.
